title: Practice: Triage and Data Handling
objective: By the end of this lesson you can mark true-positive candidates in an event table, assign severity and escalation, and choose handling for data items by sensitivity.

blocks.text: Operations questions give you a queue, not a lecture: five lines, one of which is a real breach, and a clock. The two drills here train the eyes-on part — marking the rows that matter — and the judgment half that decides how each class of data moves and rests. Both are exam skills you can only get by doing rows.

Below is one hour of a night queue. For each row: validate, scope in one phrase, assign severity, and mark the next action. Then name the row that needs hierarchical escalation, meaning authority, not more skill.

rows: IDS: known malware signature on host TEST-VM-07
Inside the approved vulnerability-scan window; source is the scan engine
Auth: 220 failed logins then a success on FIN-SRV-02, then a new admin account 'svc_helper' appears
Finance server; no change ticket matches the account
User seen in Bangkok at 09:00; attempt from overseas 20 minutes later; blocked by policy
User report: phishing email in an inbox, unread
One recipient so far; sender domain is a lookalike of the mail provider
Ops: nightly backup job failed once, retry succeeded
Logs show a storage timeout; the second attempt wrote the full set

blocks.title: Mark the true-positive candidates
steps: For each of the five rows, write real, suspicious, benign, or operational, plus the severity band you would assign.
For every real or suspicious row, give the next action and the scope question you would ask first.
Name the row that needs hierarchical escalation and say which decision belongs to management rather than analysts.
blocks.expected: 01:12 benign — approved scan matches the signature; close as documented, tune the rule to expect the scan engine; severity low. 01:40 real — high to critical: credentials worked and a new admin exists on a finance server; contain the account, scope what it touched; this row needs hierarchical escalation because finance data exposure can trigger regulatory notification decisions owned by management. 02:05 suspicious — medium: the block worked, verify with the user and check whether any other factor was satisfied; next action contact the user. 02:30 potential — medium-low: hunt other recipients, block the sender domain, ask the user not to interact; severity rises with recipient count. 02:47 operational — low: retry succeeded, but two failures in a trend threaten the recovery story, so watch it and report it with continuity metrics.

blocks.text: Four data items are moving through your area. For each: give the sensitivity label, and the handling for storage and for transit — no control, TLS in transit, encryption at rest, or both plus restricted key handling.

items: D1 — The marketing PDF destined for the public website.
D2 — An export of customer names and email addresses for a vendor campaign.
D3 — The key that decrypts the customer database.
D4 — Internal source code of the payment service.

blocks.title: Choose the handling
steps: For D1 to D4, write the sensitivity label and the handling for storage and transit.
Say which item carries the worst blast radius if it leaks, and which control does the most work in your answer.
Add the one extra rule for D3 that makes key handling different from data handling.
blocks.expected: D1 public — no control beyond integrity of the upload; publish as intended. D2 confidential personal data — TLS in transit and encryption at rest, plus the smallest extract that serves the campaign; the vendor contract covers processing. D3 restricted — the key is the crown: encrypt at rest in a vault or HSM, restricted access with dual control, rotation on schedule, and never in the same store as the data it protects. D4 internal or confidential — TLS in transit, encryption at rest, repository access by role. Worst blast radius: D3, because possessing it converts encrypted customer data into readable customer data everywhere at once. The extra rule: keys get rotation and dual control — losing one must not be forever, and one person alone must never hold the power.

blocks.title: On the exam
blocks.text: Triage asks validate before escalate; severity weighs impact, urgency, and asset value. Anything that can require regulator notification, spending, or public statements goes up the hierarchy, not just to specialists. Data handling scales with sensitivity: public needs integrity, personal data needs TLS plus encryption at rest, and keys need vault-level care with rotation and dual control.

blocks.title: Lab: Walk the Phishing Triage
blocks.description: Step frame by frame from 'email arrives' to 'reported to security', with one decision the frames grade you on. Full design: labs/phishing-triage-walkthrough.lab.en.md.

cheatsheet: Triage each row: validate, scope, severity, then escalate or close with a written reason.
Benign rows still get closed with a documented reason that feeds detection tuning.
Failed logins that turn successful plus a new admin account on a finance server is a high-to-critical real incident.
Hierarchical escalation carries the decisions management owns: regulator notification, spending, public statements.
Handling scales with sensitivity: public needs integrity, personal data needs TLS plus encryption at rest, and keys live in a vault with rotation and dual control.

checkpoint.prompt: A SIEM alert fires during the approved vulnerability-scan window, and the source address matches the scan engine. What is the correct triage outcome?

choices.A: Escalate to the CISO before touching anything
choices.B: Close as a documented false positive and tune the rule to expect scheduled scans
choices.C: Ignore the alert and move on without a record

checkpoint.explanation: Validation against context shows an approved activity: close with a written reason and tune the rule so scheduled scans stop generating noise. Silent ignoring is the habit triage exists to prevent, and reimage or escalation is disproportionate for a validated scan.

checkpoint.prompt: A vendor campaign needs customer names and email addresses exported from the CRM. Which handling fits?

choices.A: Plain CSV over email; the vendor is trusted
choices.B: Encrypt at rest only; transit is the vendor's problem
choices.C: TLS in transit, encryption at rest, and the smallest extract that serves the campaign
choices.D: Send the full customer table to be safe

checkpoint.explanation: Personal data gets protection in both states — TLS while it moves and encryption where it rests — and minimization limits what any single leak exposes. Trust in the vendor sets contract terms; it never removes the controls.

checkpoint.prompt: During an incident, analysts confirm that customer personal data may have been copied, which could trigger a regulatory notification duty. Who must be brought in beyond the technical specialists?

choices.A: Only the network team, to block the attacker
choices.B: Nobody until systems are fully restored
choices.C: The marketing team, to prepare a statement
choices.D: Management via hierarchical escalation, because notification and legal decisions belong to them

checkpoint.explanation: Decisions with legal exposure, regulator notification, spending, or public statements sit with management authority, so hierarchical escalation runs beside the technical response. Waiting for full restoration can blow a legal notification deadline.
